title: Choose your portfolio's visual world
question: The roll assigned Dada Assemblage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dada Assemblage
options.thesis: A portfolio built from tram tickets, torn newsprint, and mixed type — a found object rather than a layout.
options.viewport: A full-bleed collage of scraps at angles, the product name assembled from raid type, a printer's fist pointing at nothing in particular.
options.risk: Reads chaotic when the angles are not calibrated; the composition must feel found, not random.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: A working plate where every element registers against one off-centre calibrated rail, colour survives only as hairline emission lines.
options.viewport: A charcoal continuum crossed by needle-thin bright lines, every legend at the same tiny size, one sodium pair doubled and standing brighter than anything near it.
options.risk: Requires precise calibration; the rail must feel scientific, not decorative.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.thesis: Six luminous gauges hold a pilot's trust through cloud with nothing outside the glass.
options.viewport: A fixed constellation of instruments, each owning one truth; the cross-check sweep is the reading order.
options.risk: Reads as novelty when the gauges are not functional; each must show real data.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: A seamless cyclorama passing from black night through cobalt and rose into white day, where light alone creates an infinite horizon.
options.viewport: The curved wall begins as depthless black; a low cobalt band appears, rose gathers above it, and the actors acquire shadows before the stage becomes day.
options.risk: Requires careful gradient work; the transitions must feel atmospheric, not gradient-template.

options.label: Illuminated Initial
options.thesis: A single illuminated initial growing into a margin of gold leaf, blue vine, beasts, and tiny narrative scenes.
options.viewport: A red letter opens into a gold chamber; a blue vine escapes its stem, circles three lines of text, and ends in a fox playing a lute.
options.risk: Requires intricate vector work; the ornament must feel hand-crafted, not clip-art.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
options.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
